title: The Second Wave
subtitle: Cascadia Rupture, Tsunami Evacuation & Message Discipline

brief.userPrompt: Tuesday 13 April 2027, spring break, Pacific Daylight Time. The exercise starts at 10:00 with the Marlow County EOC (Director Gwen Halvorsen, Tsunami and Warning Coordinator Priya Natarajan, PIO Dale Whitcomb) in normal status and about 3,800 visitors in the tsunami zone. At 10:14 a magnitude 9.0 earthquake ruptures the Cascadia Subduction Zone about 80 km west of Port Alder; a ShakeAlert alert reaches the 911 center and some phones with seconds of warning at the coast and the first magnitude estimate is lower than the final one. Shaking at intensity IX lasts over four minutes; power fails across the county, cell service degrades within the hour, and three of the 18 tsunami sirens (two in Port Alder and one at the state park) do not sound. At about 10:19 the National Tsunami Warning Center issues a Tsunami Warning for the Oregon coast with first arrival at Port Alder around 10:36 to 10:40; the first wave at the harbor tide gauge is observed at 10:38 and later waves are larger. Pressure points: the county must order XL and XXL evacuation without waiting for any message and keep every message to the same zone names and the same magnitude; Marlow Coast Community Hospital (25 beds) is evacuating non-ambulatory patients to the Kellerton Station 3 apron; Port Alder Elementary School (210 students) walks to Spruce Hill and reunification at Marlow Coast High School; Cedar Court assisted living (48 residents) needs vans and will not make the assembly area in time; the 1936 Highway 101 Alder River bridge is damaged and carries the gas main; the Neskin grade on Highway 6 is blocked by a landslide; Cape Marlow PUD reports about 14,500 meters out; a viral post says the tsunami is over after the first wave and people begin to walk back to the harbor; the Harbor Master asks whether to send boats to deep water with 20 minutes left; the 911 center at 118 Front Street floods and moves to the EOC backup; the first ShakeMap and PAGER estimates are revised twice; at 11:52 a magnitude 7.6 aftershock hits and the USGS aftershock forecast is released; the Building Official must prioritize placards for the hospital, the 911 center, the shelter at Marlow Coast High School and downtown masonry, and the green placard must not be read as a guarantee against aftershocks; the NTWC warning remains in effect and the county decides when to give a return order. Decisions the exercise should record: early warning actions taken at the hospital, fire stations and school with the time completed; evacuation orders and their time against the first wave; tsunami message upgrades and the county message level; road and bridge closures; building placards; public statements. The SimCell plays the National Tsunami Warning Center, the USGS earthquake information center and seismic network, Oregon Emergency Management, ODOT District 2, the Coast Guard, neighboring Tillamook and Lincoln counties, Cape Marlow PUD, the Red Cross, the ARES amateur radio group, reporters and residents.
audience: Fire District and Sheriff Field Operations
constraints: Every county email address uses the exercise domain marlowcountyor.example; outside parties use fictional domains; never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

Tsunami messages follow the National Tsunami Warning Center message levels (Warning, Advisory, Watch, Information Statement) and are marked as exercise products; the county never upgrades or cancels an NTWC message; earthquake products give magnitude and intensity as ranges or labeled versions and aftershock chances as probabilities; times are Pacific Daylight Time.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; the National Tsunami Warning Center, USGS, Oregon Emergency Management, ODOT, the Coast Guard, utilities, hospital and school staff, the Red Cross, reporters and residents are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Acting on shaking rather than waiting for a message; one consistent message (same zone names, same magnitude) while magnitude, ShakeMap and PAGER products keep changing; protecting people who cannot self-evacuate; and holding the evacuation until the county gives a deliberate return order while later waves are larger.
overview.threat: At 10:14 PDT on Tuesday 13 April 2027, during spring break, a magnitude 9.0 earthquake ruptures the Cascadia Subduction Zone about 80 km west of Port Alder. ShakeAlert gives the coast only seconds of warning, and the first automatic magnitude is lower than the final reviewed value. Shaking of intensity IX (MMI) lasts more than four minutes and knocks out power across the county. Three of the 18 tsunami sirens do not sound, cell service degrades, the 1936 Highway 101 Alder River bridge and the gas main it carries are damaged, and a landslide blocks the Highway 6 Neskin grade. At about 10:19 the National Tsunami Warning Center issues a Tsunami Warning for the Oregon coast with first arrival at Port Alder around 10:36 to 10:40. The first wave reaches the harbor tide gauge at 10:38 and later waves are larger. A magnitude 7.6 aftershock follows at 11:52.
overview.operationalImpact:
At STARTEX (10:00) the Marlow County EOC is in normal status and about 3,800 spring-break visitors are in the tsunami zone. After the 10:14 rupture:
- **Early warning:** the 911 center and some phones get the ShakeAlert alert only seconds before shaking. Fire station bay doors, hospital elevators and the school drop-cover-hold-on bell must be confirmed and logged with completion times.
- **Sirens and alerts:** two sirens in Port Alder and one at the state park stay silent. As cell service fails within the hour, MarlowAlert and the county WEA reach fewer people.
- **Hospital:** Marlow Coast Community Hospital (25 beds, inside the XL zone) walks ambulatory patients uphill and drives non-ambulatory patients to the Kellerton Station 3 apron.
- **School:** 210 Port Alder Elementary students walk to the Spruce Hill assembly area, and parents then call about reunification at Marlow Coast High School.
- **Cedar Court:** the assisted-living facility calls for vans for 48 residents who cannot reach the assembly area before the first wave.
- **Harbor:** with about 20 minutes left, the Harbor Master asks whether to send boats to deep water.
- **911 center:** the primary center at 118 Front Street floods and telecommunicators move to the backup positions at the EOC in the middle of the call surge.
- **Utilities and roads:** Cape Marlow PUD reports about 14,500 meters out. The Alder River bridge and Neskin grade closures cut Port Alder off to the south and east.
- **Rumor:** a viral post says the tsunami ended after the first wave, and people start walking back toward the harbor.
- **Changing products:** ShakeMap and PAGER versions are revised twice and the magnitude changes, which puts the county's numbers at risk of drifting.
- **Aftershock (11:52):** the magnitude 7.6 aftershock and the USGS aftershock forecast send the Building Official to placard the hospital, the 911 backup, the Marlow Coast High School shelter and downtown masonry. Residents read a green placard as meaning "safe."
- **Return order:** the NTWC warning stays in effect, and the county must decide when, and whether, to issue a return order.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to activate the Marlow County EOC at Full Activation and order evacuation of the whole XL and XXL tsunami zones from the first strong-shaking report, before the 10:19 NTWC Tsunami Warning arrives, and to commit transport for Cedar Court and the hospital's non-ambulatory patients and give the Harbor Master an answer on boats inside the 20-minute window.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to keep one consistent public message across the PIO, the Warning position and 911, using the same zone names and a labeled, versioned magnitude, while ShakeMap, PAGER and the magnitude are revised, three sirens are silent, MarlowAlert and WEA reach fewer people as cell service fails, and the viral post saying the tsunami ended after the first wave spreads.

objectives.name: Operational Coordination
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to move 911 call-taking from the flooding Port Alder primary center to the backup positions at the EOC during the call surge, and to coordinate Fire District and Sheriff field units on door-to-door warning, access control and the closures that cut off the Highway 101 Alder River bridge and the Highway 6 Neskin grade.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to apply county doctrine after the M 7.6 aftershock: set ATC-20 placarding priorities (hospital, 911 backup, Marlow Coast High School shelter, Front Street masonry), state the USGS aftershock forecast as probabilities while making clear a green INSPECTED placard is not a guarantee, and decide a deliberate local return order while the NTWC warning stays in effect and later waves are larger, without changing the NTWC message itself.

roles.name: MCEM Director (EM Director / EOC Command)
roles.team: Team A: EM Director / EOC Command
roles.description: Owns overall direction from the EOC Command position: Full Activation, evacuation priorities, the local emergency declaration and the state request, and the timing of any return order.
standingOrders: Shaking Is the Warning: activate and order the XL and XXL zones on the shaking report; never wait for an NTWC message.
People Who Cannot Walk First: vans, vehicles and staff go to the hospital, Cedar Court and the school before anything else.
No Early Return: the largest wave is often not the first; nobody goes back toward the harbor until you give a deliberate return order.
Stay in Your Lane: the county adds local instruction but never upgrades, downgrades or cancels an NTWC message.

roles.name: Tsunami and Warning Coordinator
roles.team: Team B: Tsunami and Warning Coordinator
roles.description: Owns tsunami messages and evacuation orders: sirens, MarlowAlert, WEA and EAS, the zone names used in every message, and monitoring of NTWC messages and the harbor tide gauge.
standingOrders: Send Now: issue the evacuation order for the named zones on strong shaking; fix the wording later.
Same Words Every Time: use the exact zone names and the latest labeled magnitude version in every alert.
Fill the Gaps: when a siren or cell site is silent, ask the field for door-to-door, loudspeaker or radio coverage instead of assuming the message got through.
Gauge Over Rumor: report observed wave arrivals as observations and never state wave heights before the gauge or a buoy shows them.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Owns public statements, media, social posts, rumor control and parent reunification messaging, consistent with the Warning position and the EOC.
standingOrders: Truth Over Reassurance: say plainly that more waves are coming and are often larger; never imply it is over.
One Voice: clear every number (magnitude version, zone, times) with the Warning Coordinator before it goes out.
Kill the Rumor Fast: answer the false 'it's over' post within minutes on every channel still working.
Green Is Not Safe: every placard and aftershock message says a green placard is no guarantee against later aftershocks.

roles.name: Marlow County Communications (911) Supervisor
roles.description: Manages 911 call-taking and dispatch, including the move from the Port Alder primary center to the backup positions at the EOC during the call surge.
standingOrders: Get Out First: telecommunicators leave the primary center for the backup positions at the EOC; the call surge does not justify staying in the zone.
Triage Calls: callers in the zone are told to go uphill now; dispatch is saved for people who cannot move themselves.
Log Everything: record times for the ShakeAlert alert, bay doors, elevators, the school bell and the transfer to backup.
Feed the EOC: pass reports of collapse, people trapped and people walking back toward the harbor to Command right away.

roles.name: Port Alder Fire District Chief (Fire District and Sheriff Field Operations)
roles.team: Team E: Fire District and Sheriff Field Operations
roles.description: Manages Fire District and Sheriff field units for search and rescue, door-to-door warning, evacuation help, access control and keeping people out of the zone.
standingOrders: Crews Above the Line: no unit works in the inundation zone after the time of first arrival; rescue resumes only on Command's word.
Trust the Field: if the board and what you see disagree, report what you see and act on it.
Hold the Perimeter: deputies stop people going back toward the harbor until the county's return order, whatever social media says.

roles.name: Building Official (Building Official and Public Works)
roles.team: Team F: Building Official and Public Works
roles.description: Owns ATC-20 building safety placards and inspection priorities, and with the Public Works Director, county road and route status and closures.
standingOrders: Priority List: inspect the hospital and 911 backup, then the shelter school, Fire stations, EOC and Front Street masonry, then houses.
Date and Sign: every placard carries the date and inspector's name; reassess after any aftershock of M 6 or more.
Closed Until Inspected: the Alder River bridge and Neskin grade stay closed until an inspection reopens them; publish one route list every hour on the hour.
Coordinate, Don't Assume: closures on state highways go through ODOT; the Sheriff controls access.

phases.title: Four Minutes of Shaking
phases.goal: Tests whether Command and the Warning Coordinator act on strong shaking alone: Full Activation and an XL/XXL evacuation order before the 10:19 NTWC message, ShakeAlert actions logged, and transport committed for the people who cannot walk out inside the 20-minute window.
beats: (10:05) Noise item while the EOC is in normal status: the NWS Portland office relays a routine marine statement, and a State Parks campground host asks whether the spring-break beach bonfire permit still stands. Neither has anything to do with what follows.

(10:14) The ShakeAlert alert reaches the 911 center and some phones only seconds before MMI IX shaking that lasts more than four minutes, and power fails countywide. The Warning Coordinator starts the early warning action log (SOP-EQ-02 2): Station 1, 2 and 3 bay doors, hospital elevators, the Port Alder Elementary drop, cover, hold on bell, and the Marlow & Pacific dispatcher's stop order for the Alder River trestle. Each entry needs its completion time.

(10:16–10:19) First strong-shaking reports come in. Command must declare Full Activation and order evacuation of the whole XL and XXL zones at once (EOP 6.1–6.2) before the NTWC Tsunami Warning arrives over the Position 2 Weather Wire at about 10:19, which gives first arrival at Port Alder as 10:36–10:40 and an automatic magnitude lower than the final value. Field units report that two Port Alder sirens and the state park siren are silent.

(10:20–10:25) Two calls arrive within minutes. Cedar Court asks for 4 vans for 48 residents, 10 of them in wheelchairs. Harbor Master Luis Ferreira asks whether the 42 boats should go to deep water, with about 20 minutes left and a plan rule of more than 60 minutes. Meanwhile the hospital moves non-ambulatory patients to the Kellerton Station 3 apron and 210 students walk to Spruce Hill.

(10:30–10:45) The Port Alder primary 911 center starts flooding during the call surge, and the 911 Supervisor must move telecommunicators to the backup positions at the EOC. At 10:38 the harbor tide gauge records the first wave arriving, and the Warning position posts it on the WebEOC Tsunami Status board.

phases.title: The Larger Waves
phases.goal: Tests message discipline while products and field reports keep changing: one set of zone names and a labeled, versioned magnitude across the PIO, Warning and 911; field reports kept separate from modeled estimates; route closures carried out; and the 11:52 aftershock absorbed.
beats: (11:00) The USGS event summary is revised to a higher reviewed magnitude, and ShakeMap and PAGER come out as version 2 with a red PAGER alert. Planning must date each version in the sitrep and keep PAGER estimates separate from Sheriff, Fire and Public Works field reports (SOP-EQ-02 3). The PIO's draft still carries the old automatic magnitude.

(11:10) Red herring: a ham radio relay reports that the Spruce Hill assembly area is under water and students are missing. A field check finds the assembly area dry and all 210 students accounted for. The bad report has already reached parents calling 911 about reunification at Marlow Coast High School.

(11:15) Visual confirmation: the harbor tide gauge trace and a Fire District photo from Spruce Hill show a later wave reaching higher than the first. Field units confirm damage to the 1936 Highway 101 Alder River bridge and a gas odor at its main, and report the landslide on the Highway 6 Neskin grade. Command closes both under EOP 6.4 and sends the closures to ODOT District 2 and the Road Status board.

(11:30) A viral post says the tsunami ended after the first wave, and the Sheriff reports people walking back toward the harbor. A coastal reporter wants a quote by 11:45. MarlowAlert and WEA delivery drops as cell service fails, and Cape Marlow PUD reports about 14,500 meters out.

(11:52) An M 7.6 aftershock (automatic) hits. 911 backup positions take a new surge of calls, and the hospital asks the Building Official to check the Station 3 apron and its own wing before patients are moved again.

phases.title: Hold the High Ground
phases.goal: Tests the exercise's one decision point: whether to keep the evacuation in place while the NTWC warning stands and later waves are larger, or allow a limited early return. The phase also tests mutual aid, the local declaration and care for people who cannot help themselves.
beats: (12:05) DECISION POINT: Pacific Reach Seafoods, the hospital and about 3,800 cold visitors on Spruce Hill press for re-entry to the waterfront and the Alder River flats. Holding the evacuation means overcrowded assembly areas, Cedar Court residents exposed outside, patients on the Station 3 apron and an economic cost. Allowing early return risks people being in the zone for a larger wave while the NTWC warning stays in effect. The county may set local instructions but may not cancel or downgrade the NTWC message (STWE 2).

(12:15) Command makes the local emergency declaration within the four-hour window (EOP 6.5) and asks for a state declaration through the OEM Regional Coordination Center. Liaison requests mutual aid from Tillamook and Lincoln counties and Coast Guard air support. Players must state who is in command, given that both highways are cut and outside help is planned at 72 hours or more.

(12:25) Access and functional needs: Cedar Court has 2 of 4 vans and 10 wheelchair users waiting. Ten students at Marlow Coast High School have no parent who can reach them. Staff from south of the Alder River bridge cannot get to the EOC.

(12:40) The USGS releases its first aftershock forecast through the state RCC Duty Seismologist. The PIO must put out probability ranges by 13:00 (EOP 6.6) using the same zone names and the current magnitude version, and correct the 'tsunami is over' rumor again across the WebEOC boards, 911 scripts and the satellite and Starlink channels.

phases.title: Placards and Return
phases.goal: Tests ATC-20 placarding priorities, partner notifications and a deliberate phased return decision made by local officials, including the message that a green placard is not a guarantee against aftershocks.
beats: (13:05) Building Official Ines Calloway sends inspectors and SEA volunteer engineers out in SOP-EQ-02 4 priority order for the sites above the line: the 911 backup at the EOC, the Marlow Coast High School shelter, the Fire stations, then the roughly 40 Front Street unreinforced masonry buildings. Placards come back dated: the 911 backup and the high school INSPECTED, Station 3 RESTRICTED USE; the hospital and Front Street are observed from outside only, because the Warning is still in effect.

(13:20) Hurdle: the Marlow Coast High School shelter reaches capacity and its generator fails. Red Cross Oregon cannot deliver cots because both highways are cut. Residents post that the green INSPECTED placard means the shelter is 'safe forever', and the PIO must correct this.

(13:35) Notifications: Lifelines and Shelters status goes to OEM, DOGAMI and ODOT District 2. Cape Marlow Natural Gas begins its post-event survey around the Alder River bridge main, and PUD reports its first staged restorations. If an M 6+ aftershock occurs, the plan requires reinspection.

(13:35) The OEM duty officer reports that the NTWC has replaced the Warning with an Advisory (Message Number 7, 13:34). Command decides whether to start any phased local return and tests it against the STWE 8 criteria, with the harbor and Alder River flats the last to reopen. The aftershock caveat goes into every message, and the county's wording must not restate or alter the NTWC message.

(14:00) ENDEX: Command gives a final sitrep with the versioned magnitude (Event Summary version 3, ShakeMap and PAGER version 2), the open closures and the early warning action log completed for the hot wash.

msel.event: Three needs reach the EOC within five minutes. (1) Radio Call relayed by Deputy 9 from the Cedar Court administrator: "Only two of the four vans made it. msel.from: Marlow Coast High School shelter team lead; American Red Cross Oregon region; Port Alder residents (Facebook)
msel.event: Three items arrive within four minutes. (1) Phone Call from the Marlow Coast High School shelter team lead: "We're at 400 registered in the gym, which is our limit, and 60 more are standing in the rain at the door. The generator quit at 13:14. The fuel looked fine, but it won't restart. No lights, no heat, and the family reunification list is on a laptop with 20 percent battery left." (2) Email Forward to eoc@marlowcountyor.example from the American Red Cross Oregon region (logistics@redcross-oregon.example), 13:17: "We have 500 cots and 1,000 blankets staged in Salem but cannot route a truck: Highway 101 is closed at the Alder River bridge and Highway 6 at the Neskin grade. Earliest delivery depends on the ODOT route list or a Coast Guard sling load." (3) Post (@PortAlderMom_Kris, Facebook, 13:15) with a photo of the green placard on the high school door: "GOOD NEWS: the county stamped the high school INSPECTED = SAFE. Engineers say it can't fall down so bring your whole family and the dogs, it's the safest building in the county now even if there's another big one 🙏 #PortAlderStrong #Tsunami" It has 640 shares, and replies are asking whether the Front Street shops with green tags are 'safe to reopen.'
msel.expectedAction: The PIO corrects the post on every working channel: an INSPECTED (green) placard means no apparent hazard was found at the time of inspection, and it is no guarantee against later aftershocks. The PIO also explains that the shelter is full and gives the overflow site. Command assigns a generator or fuel tech through Public Works or the PUD, opens an overflow site such as the Kellerton EOC area or the Station 3 bays, and makes the cots a resource request to OEM and the Coast Guard. Fire helps move the 60 people at the door. The green-placard post is the misinformation; the shelter capacity, generator and Red Cross logistics items are true and need real action.

msel.event: (1) Phone Call on the RCC bridge line from the OEM duty officer: "Marlow County, we need your Lifelines and Shelters status by 14:00 for the state situation report. DOGAMI is asking for observed inundation limits, and ODOT District 2 wants your county route list to match theirs on 101 and 6. Please send each one route, shelter and lifeline list with a time stamp." (2) Radio Call from the Cape Marlow Natural Gas crew lead, relayed by Deputy 14: "We've isolated the main at the north valve. Starting our leak survey along the 101 Alder River bridge now, from the north bank only. Readings near the south abutment are still at 30 percent LEL, so keep everyone back 300 feet." (3) Phone Call from PUD Operations Manager Rafael Ibarra: "First staged restoration: Substation 1 is inspected and the Kellerton feeder was re-energized at 13:30. That covers the EOC and Station 3, about 1,200 meters, so roughly 13,300 are still out. High school feeder is pending a line patrol, maybe 16:00. Substations 2 and 3 have no estimate." (4) Alarm, ShakeAlert at the EOC, 13:31:40: "Earthquake! Drop, Cover, Hold On." PNSN automatic solution, 13:33: M 5.4 (automatic), about 70 km W of Port Alder. Light-to-moderate shaking in Kellerton for about 10 seconds. (5) The OEM duty officer adds on the same call: the NTWC has replaced the Warning with a Tsunami Advisory, Message Number 7, issued 13:34 PDT, and asks what the county will do about its own return order.
msel.expectedAction: DECISION POINT: Command decides whether any return order is issued under the Advisory, states which STWE 8 return criteria it tested, and tells the partners and the public through the PIO. The Building Official and the Public Works Director send one time-stamped route list (Highway 101 Alder River bridge and Highway 6 Neskin grade CLOSED, with the basis) consistent with ODOT District 2, and keep the gas exclusion zone with the Sheriff. Command approves the Lifelines and Shelters report to OEM, keeping field observations separate from modeled estimates. The Building Official notes the M 5.4 is automatic and below the M 6 reassessment trigger, watches for a revised magnitude, and spot-checks the hospital and Station 3 canopy. The Warning Coordinator updates the boards to Message Number 7 without restating or altering it (STWE 2).

FOPS left the Alder River bridge open to traffic or sent units below the line after I-10, and the stranded Cedar Court wheelchair users in I-16 were not assigned a vehicle.
metrics.pass: 911S ordered Port Alder staff out at I-06, rolled calls to the EOC backup positions and logged the transfer time and gap. FOPS assigned deputies to bridge access control and the gas standoff at I-10, sent loudspeaker and door-to-door coverage to the three silent sirens at I-11b, and moved the Cedar Court residents with a crew that stayed above the line at I-16.
metrics.excellence: 911S started moving staff to the backup positions as soon as the 10:19 arrival time was known, before I-06 forced it, and asked Command for mutual aid telecommunicators before the I-16 relief shortfall. FOPS put door-to-door teams on Front Street, the harbor and the campground right after I-02 and pre-staged a perimeter on Hemlock before the I-11 walk-back.

metrics.name: Evacuation Decision Making and Hazard Judgement
metrics.fail: DIR waited for the I-03 NTWC Tsunami Warning, or for a later message, before ordering the XL and XXL evacuation. At I-04 DIR gave no answer on Cedar Court transport or the boats, or ordered the fleet to sea. At I-14 DIR allowed cannery or hospital-basement re-entry while the warning was still active.
metrics.pass: DIR declared Full Activation and ordered evacuation of the whole XL and XXL zones on the I-02 shaking report, and logged the order time against the I-03 message. At I-04 DIR sent the first vehicles to Cedar Court and confirmed that vessels stay in port. At I-14 DIR held the evacuation and refused re-entry while the warning was active and the gauge was above 0.3 m.
metrics.excellence: DIR issued the XL/XXL order and committed transport for Cedar Court and the hospital's non-ambulatory patients within minutes of I-02, before the calls in I-04 came in. At I-14 DIR held the line and also had a care plan ready (patients off the apron, warming, oxygen by air or from the upland west wing), using the larger observed waves from I-10 and I-13 as the reason.

metrics.name: Public Communication and Message Discipline
metrics.fail: PIO gave the radio station in I-05 an unlabeled or uncleared magnitude or a guessed wave height, posted the stale M 7.3 draft after I-08, or let the I-11 'tsunami is over' rumor and the I-18 chyron go uncorrected for more than one cycle. metrics.pass: PIO cleared one labeled, versioned magnitude with the TWC before every release (I-05, I-08, I-17). PIO gave wave heights only as timed gauge observations and corrected the I-11 and I-18 misinformation on every working channel, saying more waves are expected and are often larger. The 911S updated the caller script to the same zone names and the same magnitude version.
metrics.excellence: PIO and TWC set up a single versioned message board for the PIO, Warning and 911 positions before I-08, so the M 8.9 and M 9.0 revisions spread without errors. PIO sent out 'later waves are often larger' and 'parents do not drive into the zone' messages before the I-05 parent post and the I-11 rumor. PIO also contacted the Coast Guard and the TV station before the I-18 one o'clock broadcast.

metrics.name: Use of Doctrine
metrics.fail: Players made the I-14 return decision and the I-20 placard priorities without citing any plan section. TWC changed or 'cancelled' the NTWC message level locally. PIO told the public that the green placard in I-21 meant 'safe', or rounded the 30 percent M 7 forecast in I-17 to 'unlikely'.

BO applied the SOP-EQ-02 section 4 inspection order at I-12 and I-20. PIO stated the I-17 forecast as probabilities with its window and explained at I-21 that an INSPECTED placard is not a guarantee.
metrics.excellence: Players cited section numbers without prompting, before the inject asked for them: EOP 6.1–6.2 and STWE 5 at the first shaking, SOP-EQ-02 section 3 for versioned products, SOP-EQ-02 section 4 at I-12 before the engineers asked at I-20, and STWE 8 to set a phased local return order. hotwash.methodDescription: 3-Up, 3-Down asks the room for three things that went well and three things that broke or failed during the exercise. Go around the room one team at a time (Command, Warning/PIO, 911, Fire/Sheriff, Shelter/Hospital, Building) and write every answer on the whiteboard in two columns before anyone discusses them, so the loudest team doesn't set the list.

questions.text: The shaking lasted more than four minutes and the NTWC Tsunami Warning didn't arrive until about 10:19. Who on your team ordered evacuation of the whole XL and XXL zones, and when? Was it on the strong-shaking report or only after the message came in? STWE 2 says nobody waits for the message. If you waited, what were you waiting for? Within that 20-minute window, when did you commit transport for the Cedar Court residents and the hospital's non-ambulatory patients, and when did the Harbor Master get an answer on the boats?

At I-18, the TV chyron said the 'Coast Guard says tsunami threat passing'. At the same moment, the 911 backup caller script still read 'M 8.0' and people at the Spruce Hill aid station were packing up. Earlier, at I-11, the @SurfDadOregon post and the Coast Ledger reporter asked whether the first wave was the worst. When did the PIO, the Warning position and 911 last check that they were using the same zone names and the same labeled, versioned magnitude? Who owned updating the caller script, and what did you tell Deputy 9's crowd of 40 and the Channel 8 reporter while the gauge showed later waves were larger?

At I-14, three requests arrived within four minutes: the seafood plant manager wanted four people on the Alder River flats 'while the water's way out', the CMO wanted staff sent back into the hospital basement for oxygen, and 3,800 people on Spruce Hill were threatening to walk down. NTWC Message Number 4 still read WARNING. Did you treat the drawdown as a safe window or as a sign of the next wave? What did you give each of them instead of a 'yes', for example oxygen from Station 3 or shelter and warmth for the Cedar Court residents? What would have let you make that decision faster?

At I-10, the tide gauge showed +3.6 m at 11:06 compared with +2.4 m at the first wave. The Engine 31 photo put the water two blocks past Front Street. Deputy 14 reported that the 101 bridge abutment had dropped a foot and the gas smell was getting stronger, and ODOT reported the Highway 6 Neskin slide. Did you use those reports to reposition field units, access control and closures, or did they just become log entries? How did the 911 move from the flooding primary center to the EOC backup positions hold up during the call surge? At I-22, how quickly did your route list match ODOT's for the OEM sitrep?

At I-21, the @PortAlderMom_Kris post told people the green INSPECTED placard on the high school meant it 'can't fall down'. The shelter was already at its 400 limit with no generator, and the Red Cross truck couldn't get past the 101 and 6 closures. Then the M 5.4 ShakeAlert at 13:31 hit at I-22. How did you set ATC-20 placarding priorities after the M 7.6? Did the PIO, the Building Official and the shelter manager quote the same USGS aftershock forecast issuance, as probabilities with the time it was issued, as SOP-EQ-02 section 7 requires? Was the deliberate local return order you gave or held back stated as your own local instruction, without appearing to change the NTWC warning?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Oregon Emergency Management (OEM) Regional Coordination Center duty officer (and, on request, Tillamook County Emergency Management for mutual aid)
simcellScripts.trigger: Players call the RCC bridge line to request state resources, a state declaration, Coast Guard or Red Cross support, or mutual aid; or the RCC calls in at I-15 (12:15) and I-22 (13:35).
hardQuestions: Do you have a signed local emergency declaration? No? Then I can't take a state declaration request to the Governor's office. Who is your incident commander, and who signs if your Director can't be reached?
Every coastal county from Clatsop to Curry is on this line. What are your top three priorities, in order? 'Everything' is not an order.
Your route list says 101 is 'restricted' and ODOT District 2 says 'closed.' Which is it, and when was it stamped? I need one route, shelter and lifeline list with a time stamp by 14:00.
Tillamook here: our own waterfront is under water. We can send a 6-person CERT team and one ambulance, but how do they get to you? We can't cross the Neskin grade.
concessions: Once the county gives a signed declaration and names the IC and a successor signer, the RCC takes the state declaration request to the Governor's office and logs Marlow County's resource request with a tracking number.

Once the county sends a ranked list of priorities with locations and patient counts, the RCC passes it to the Coast Guard helicopter tasking and asks the Red Cross about a sling load of cots and blankets.
Tillamook commits its CERT team and ambulance once the county names a staging point and an open route, as shown on the county's hourly route list.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: NWS National Tsunami Warning Center (Palmer, AK) duty scientist, reached through the NWS Portland forecast office
simcellScripts.trigger: The Warning Coordinator or Director calls to ask whether the warning still stands, how big the waves will be, when it will be cancelled, or whether it is safe to let people return (most likely around I-11, I-14, I-18 or I-19).
hardQuestions: Which message are you reading? We're on Message Number 6. If your desk still has Number 1 or 4, you're behind.
We lost your Port Alder gauge at 10:41. What has it shown since it came back, with times, and is that observed or estimated?
I can't give you a wave height for the next wave, and I don't give your local all clear. That's your call. What are you basing your return decision on?
That TV chyron about the Coast Guard saying the threat is passing didn't come from us. The warning is in effect. Who is correcting it on your end?
concessions: Once the county passes observed gauge readings and the field water line with times, the duty scientist confirms the current message number and the time of the next message, and notes that the county's observations are in the next update.

If asked directly, the duty scientist explains that a downgrade to a Tsunami Advisory is possible as gauges trend down, but an Advisory still means strong currents and danger in or near the water and harbors. It does not mean the county should allow a return to the XL zone.
NWS Portland will put the county's own return-order wording on its dissemination channels only after the county sends it in writing and the NTWC message in effect allows it.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: ODOT District 2 maintenance lead / bridge section
simcellScripts.trigger: Team F (Building Official and Public Works) or the Director calls about the Highway 101 Alder River bridge, the Highway 6 Neskin grade slide, a bridge engineer, or reopening a route for Red Cross trucks or relief staff (I-10, I-16, I-21, I-22).
hardQuestions: That's a state highway, so closure is our call. Is the Sheriff physically holding both ends of the Alder River bridge? I've got reports of cars turning around at the north end.
No bridge engineer has looked at that 1936 span, and it moved about a foot at the south abutment. It stays closed until we inspect, and we can't get an engineer there by road. Can you get one to us?
Cape Marlow Natural Gas is reading 30 percent LEL near the south abutment. Who is keeping people 300 feet back while my crew works?
Your partners are getting three different route lists. Send me yours on the hour, every hour, with the basis for each closure.
concessions: Once the county sends a time-stamped route list that matches the state's status on 101 and 6, ODOT confirms it and the two agencies issue matching lists on the hour.
Once the Sheriff confirms access control at both ends of the bridge and the gas exclusion is in place, ODOT puts barricades at the north end and asks the RCC to prioritize a bridge engineer by air.
ODOT will start a geotechnical look at the Neskin grade slide from the east side, but it will give no reopening time until the geotech has seen it.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Coast Guard command center (Sector Columbia River, Astoria), relayed through the Oregon OEM RCC, plus the Port Alder Harbor Master Luis Ferreira on the Port channel
simcellScripts.trigger: Players ask for helicopter support (hypothermic or oxygen-dependent patients, Cedar Court wheelchair users, a sling load of Red Cross supplies), ask about the harbor fleet (I-04), or try to confirm the Channel 8 chyron attributed to a Coast Guard spokesperson (I-18).
hardQuestions: We have one helicopter for the whole Oregon coast and can't commit before 14:00. Send me priorities with patient counts, conditions, a landing zone and coordinates. 'Spruce Hill' is not a landing zone.
Harbor Master again. You've got 15 minutes before the wave. Do I send the 42 boats to deep water or tie up and walk my 120 cannery workers uphill? Yes or no.
We did not tell anyone to go home. We don't give the all clear on land. Who at the county is going to say that on air, and when?
Is the harbor basin closed to boats coming back in? Skippers are calling me asking whether they can return to port.
concessions: Once the county sends a ranked medevac list with a marked, cleared landing zone and a ground contact on a working radio channel, the Coast Guard tasks the helicopter to the top priority after 14:00 and considers a later sling load.
Once the PIO asks in writing, the Coast Guard public affairs office issues a statement that the Coast Guard has not cleared any return and that local officials decide when people may go back.

If the county closes the harbor and tells the Harbor Master clearly, the Coast Guard broadcasts a Safety Marine Information Broadcast telling vessels at sea to stay in deep water and not return to Port Alder.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: News media: Marlow Coast Radio 1 news director, Lena Ortiz of the Coast Ledger, and the Channel 8 Coast News newsroom
simcellScripts.trigger: The PIO picks up or returns a media call (I-05, I-11, I-18), or any player gives a number, wave height or return time that reaches the press.
hardQuestions: I go live in two minutes. My phone alert said 7.3, the tsunami warning says 8.0 and someone just read me 8.7. Give me one number I can put on air.
Is the tsunami over? People are saying the first wave was the worst. How high did the water get? Is it 30 feet?
We're quoting a Coast Guard spokesperson from Astoria saying people can start going home. Confirm a return time for our 1 o'clock or we run what we have.
Your website says the high school is INSPECTED. Is that the same as safe? People are bringing their dogs.
concessions: If the PIO gives a named spokesperson and an on-record statement with the magnitude labeled by version (for example 'M 9.0, USGS reviewed, version 3'), the outlet reads it word for word on its next break and keeps reading it until the next update.

If the county gives a written correction with a named source before the deadline, Channel 8 pulls the chyron and runs a correction that the evacuation stays in place and only local officials can order a return.
If the PIO gives observed water levels from the gauge or a field water line, labeled with times, the reporter uses those numbers instead of a guessed wave height.

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. Players are judged on how well plans, procedures and coordination hold up, not on their own performance.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. A Cascadia magnitude 9 rupture with a local tsunami, as described in EOP 2, is the planning case for Marlow County.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures, including the county EOP tsunami annex, SOP-TSU-01 and the county's warning and alerting procedures. Where a plan is silent, players say so and describe what they would do.

Players have only the information on the inject cards and in this manual. Earthquake magnitudes, ShakeMap, PAGER and tide gauge values are treated as they would be in a real event: provisional, versioned and subject to revision.
Players do not wait for confirmation from outside agencies before acting. Like the real county, they plan on no outside help reaching them for at least 72 hours.
Decisions made in one module carry into the next. Each module's situation update describes events as they reached the room, not the results of player decisions.
artificialities: Time is compressed. Each module covers one hour of event time, and between modules the facilitator jumps the clock forward (11:00, 12:00, 13:00) with a time jump card.

The SimCell plays everyone outside the room, including the National Tsunami Warning Center, the USGS and Pacific Northwest Seismic Network, the NWS Portland forecast office, Oregon OEM and its Regional Coordination Center, ODOT District 2, the Coast Guard, Tillamook County, the American Red Cross, the hospital, Cedar Court, the Port, the PUD, the media and members of the public.

Systems named in the plans are not touched during play. These include the sirens, MarlowAlert, WEA/IPAWS, the EAS, NOAA Weather Wire, CAD, WebEOC and the tide gauge feed. Players describe what they would send or do, and the SimCell reports the result.
Injects arrive on paper or on screen: calls, radio traffic, emails, social media posts, technical feeds and alarms. Every product is marked EXERCISE, and no real public message is issued.
Field units, aftershock shaking and protective actions (drop, cover, hold on) are only discussed. Nobody moves or evacuates during the exercise.

modules.narrativeMd:
**Module 1: Four Minutes of Shaking (10:00–11:00 PDT)**

It is 10:00 Pacific Daylight Time on Tuesday 13 April 2027, the middle of spring break on the Marlow County coast. The weather is overcast with light rain, 52°F, a west wind at 10 mph and a falling tide. The Marlow County EOC in Kellerton is in normal (monitoring) status. modules.narrativeMd:
**Module 2: The Larger Waves (11:00–12:00 PDT)**

It is 11:00 PDT, 46 minutes after the earthquake. ShakeAlert warned Position 2 at 10:14:02 with an automatic M 7.3. Violent shaking followed and lasted more than three and a half minutes. Commercial power failed countywide. Sirens were activated at 10:17, but the Front Street, harbor and campground sirens have stayed silent. Deputy 14 reported the Highway 101 Alder River bridge deck offset at the south abutment, with a strong smell of gas. The NTWC Tsunami Warning (Message Number 1, M 8.0 preliminary) arrived at 10:19 and gave a first arrival at Port Alder of 10:36 to 10:40. Cedar Court asked for four vans for 48 residents, and the Harbor Master asked for a decision on 42 boats and 120 cannery workers. The hospital began moving patients, and the elementary school walked its 210 students toward Spruce Hill.

By 10:30 the PIO was being asked about three different magnitudes (7.3, 8.0 and a reported 8.7), and a parents' post urged people to drive down Front Street to the school. At 10:38 the Port Alder tide gauge recorded +2.4 m, then went silent at 10:41. Water reached the Port Alder primary 911 center, and call-taking now runs from the backup positions at the Kellerton EOC with more than 60 calls in the queue.

The NTWC Warning is still in effect. Cell service is intermittent, the EOC is on generator, and nobody has seen the harbor since 10:45. Spruce Hill is crowded with evacuees in the rain, and about 180 campers are holding on the high bluff. The non-ambulatory hospital patients are on the Kellerton Station 3 apron. Media and public calls about magnitude and water height keep piling up.

**Module 3: Hold the High Ground (12:00–13:00 PDT)**

It is 12:00 PDT, 1 hour 46 minutes after the earthquake. Since 11:00 the USGS has revised the mainshock to M 8.9 (version 2, reviewed). ShakeMap version 2 estimates MMI IX at Port Alder, and PAGER version 2 is at RED. All of these are labeled modeled estimates. An ARES relay reported that the Spruce Hill assembly area was under water and children were missing. A scene photo from Engine 31 on Spruce Hill shows the water line two blocks past Front Street. When the tide gauge came back it showed +3.6 m at 11:06, larger than the first wave. The south abutment of the Highway 101 Alder River bridge has dropped about a foot, and ODOT reports a landslide across Highway 6 on the Neskin grade at about MP 9. A viral post says the tsunami is done, and about 40 people walked back toward the harbor. MarlowAlert delivered only about a third of its texts. The PUD reports nearly all 14,500 meters out, with no restoration before tomorrow.

At 11:52 an aftershock struck, M 7.6 by automatic solution, and the CAD queue jumped to 71 calls. The hospital reported a new crack in the Station 3 canopy over its patients. The NTWC Tsunami Warning remains in effect (Message Number 4, 11:45). At 11:58 the tide gauge recorded a third wave of +4.1 m, the largest so far. About 3,800 people are on Spruce Hill in cold rain at 49°F with no shelter, toilets or water. Eleven hospital patients are under the cracked canopy, and Cedar Court residents are spread along the roadside. Both highways are cut and no outside help has arrived. Pressure to go back down the hill is growing by the minute.

modules.narrativeMd:
**Module 4: Placards and Return (13:00–14:00 PDT)**

It is 13:00 PDT, 2 hours 46 minutes after the earthquake. Over the past hour the EOC has handled competing demands: a seafood plant asking to re-enter the Alder River flats, the hospital needing oxygen and blankets, and a restless crowd on Spruce Hill. The state RCC has asked for the signed local declaration. Tillamook County offered a CERT team and an ambulance it cannot get across the Neskin grade, and the Coast Guard's single helicopter is not available before 14:00. Ten Cedar Court wheelchair users were waiting at the Spruce Hill road edge, ten elementary students were still not reunified, and 911 relief staff could not reach Kellerton. A Nextdoor post claimed the Spruce Hill water tank was failing. USGS version 3 (reviewed) now gives the mainshock as M 9.0 and the largest aftershock as M 7.5. Its first aftershock forecast gives a 30 percent chance of M 7 or larger in the next week, with a warning that any large offshore aftershock can generate a new local tsunami. A regional TV chyron claimed the Coast Guard said residents may begin returning, and callers are reading it back to 911.

The NTWC Tsunami Warning is still in effect (Message Number 6, 12:45). The tide gauge shows the waves getting smaller but not stopping: +2.7 m at 12:52 and +1.4 m at 12:58. Harbor surges continue, and the Front Street water line is still rising and falling. About 3,800 people are on Spruce Hill or at the Kellerton and Marlow Coast High School sites. The 911 backup positions have 38 calls holding, and both highways remain cut. Damage reports have replaced life-safety calls: Front Street facades, the hospital east wing, the Station 3 canopy and a shelter that is filling up. Volunteer engineers from the Structural Engineers Association have reported to the EOC. Everyone wants to know which buildings are safe and when they can go home.

Sending partners one timestamped list of routes, shelters and lifelines
Setting lifeline restoration priorities with very little power available
